column1: # Per-game LFS remotes: name, endpoint, path prefix. Tab-separated.
# The blobs are not in one store. Each game has its own Forgejo repo, and stock
# git-lfs reads lfs.url from the repo-root .lfsconfig only -- which names
# KBVE/rareicon for the whole monorepo. So anything pulling or pushing another
# game's assets has to name the endpoint itself, and this is the list it names
# it from.
# The prefix is what the game owns: it is the pathspec for a pull and the scope
# for `kbve.sh -lfs <game> register`. Narrower than the game's tree means blobs
# that never upload and 404 in CI.
# Forgejo dedups content across the KBVE org, so a blob pushed to the root
# endpoint is readable through another repo once its OID is registered there.
# That is why a pull against the rareicon endpoint can succeed for a different
# game's assets, and why the right fix for a 404 is `register`, not a reroute.
